profiles.name: CRANK
profiles.tagline: SHORT-GAME GREMLIN WITH A DRIVER PROBLEM
profiles.profile: CRANK keeps showing up like a guy who can save par from the rough but still tries to fight the golf course with the big stick. The pattern is pretty clear: the driver is usually the part of the bag throwing chairs, while the wedges and putter keep dragging the card back from the ditch. That makes him dangerous in NET because he can survive a mess, manufacture a run, and ugly-win his way through chaos. The swing is volatile, but the scrambling is real, and that’s a nasty combo when the leaderboard gets stupid.

profiles.name: MattF
profiles.tagline: TEE SHOT ON A LEASH, SCORING ON FIRE
profiles.profile: MattF is what happens when a player decides fairways are optional and still shows up with enough tee-to-green juice to bully the whole room. The driver can get punchy and sloppy, but the rest of the bag keeps cashing checks like it owns the place. He’s not a one-note bomber either; when the irons and putter are both awake, the thing turns into a demolition job. The weird part is that the mess off the tee doesn’t always matter because the scoring engine underneath is just stupidly loud.

profiles.name: Dan94
profiles.tagline: APPROACH RAID WITH A SIDE OF CHAOS
profiles.profile: Dan94 is the rare guy who can absolutely carve up a course and still leave a trail of “how the hell was that not lower?” behind him. The irons do the heavy lifting, the driver brings the swagger, and the short game shows up like it got lost on the way to someone else’s round. He’s a pure shot-maker with enough firepower to win golf tournaments the ugly way, which is usually the best way. When he’s sharp, the ceiling is disgusting; when the putter gets merely okay, everybody else is basically playing for second and manners.

profiles.name: KeithK75
profiles.tagline: FIVE CLUBS OF VIOLENCE AND A SCORECARD
profiles.profile: KeithK75 plays like somebody who found the cheat code for striking the ball and then got distracted by how many birdies he could pile up. The approach game is the headline act, but the bigger story is that he doesn’t need perfect conditions to start shoving his way to the front. He can get wild, sure, but the birdie production is too steady to dismiss as a heater. This is the kind of player who makes a course look negotiable, then casually leaves the rest of the field staring at his tire tracks.

profiles.name: BigTime
profiles.tagline: IRONS DO THE BRAWLING, PUTTER DOES THE PANIC
profiles.profile: BigTime is basically a walking argument that you can survive a mediocre tee ball if the wedges are throwing daggers. The profile is all over the place in the most entertaining way: the irons are often filthy, the putter is capable of bailing out disasters, and the driver acts like it’s just there for decoration half the time. He lives in the tension between brilliant approach play and enough self-inflicted nonsense to keep things spicy. Not clean, not boring, and definitely not someone you want waking up the scoring clubs.

profiles.name: HamSammich
profiles.profile: HamSammich is the kind of golfer who can flash a real round and then immediately kick the scorecard into a ditch just to keep things interesting. There’s enough tee and putting pop here to hint at upside, but the rest of the profile has too much roughhousing and not enough restraint. When it’s bad, it gets stupid fast; when it’s decent, he can absolutely hang around because the putter and driver occasionally decide to cooperate. This is a volatile file, which is a polite way of saying the wheels can come off without warning.
